name: Finland
tagline: Forest, lake, sauna, silence — and a design tradition that came out of all four.
summary: Finland is 188,000 lakes and more forest per person than anywhere in Europe, arranged around a habit of not talking unnecessarily. The sauna is not a spa treatment here; it is where the country conducts its private life, and there are more saunas than cars. Lapland in winter is the reason most people come, and the lake district in July is the reason some come back.

season.note: July is lake weather and the whole country is at a summer cottage. February and March give reliable snow with returning daylight — better than December, which is dark and expensive. Autumn ruska, the turning of the Lapland birch, is a fortnight in mid-September.

getting_around: Trains north to Rovaniemi run overnight with car carriages. Helsinki's trams and the Suomenlinna ferry are on the same ticket. Beyond the rail line, Lapland is a car or a coach.
food: Rye bread, dense and sour, eaten with everything
Lakeside perch and vendace, fried whole
Salmiakki — salt liquorice, which is a test rather than a snack

festivals.name: Savonlinna Opera Festival, in a medieval castle

know: Sauna etiquette: naked, quiet, and you throw water on the stones yourself.
Everyman's right allows walking, berry-picking and mushrooming on almost all land.
Winter driving needs winter tyres by law, and reindeer have right of way in practice.

regions.name: Helsinki & the Southern Coast
regions.summary: A young capital of granite and sea, with a sea fortress and an archipelago at the end of the tram line.

cities.name: Helsinki
cities.summary: Neoclassical centre, brutal-modern edges, and a design district you can walk in an afternoon.
highlights: Suomenlinna: a UNESCO sea fortress on six islands, twenty minutes by ferry
Temppeliaukio, a church blasted into bedrock
Löyly and the return of the public sauna to the waterfront
The Oodi library, which lends power tools

experiences.name: A public sauna on the sea
experiences.summary: Hot, then the Baltic, then hot again. The rule is that nobody performs and nobody talks much.

experiences.name: The Design District on foot
experiences.summary: Twenty-five streets, two hundred shops and studios, and the through-line from Aalto to whoever graduated last year.

cities.name: Porvoo
cities.summary: Red ochre warehouses on a river, and Finland's second-oldest town an hour from the capital.
highlights: The riverfront shore houses, painted for a royal visit in 1809
Cobbled old town with working chocolate and glass makers
Wooden church on the hill above it

regions.name: The Lakeland
regions.summary: The blue middle of the country: 188,000 lakes, wooden cottages, and a castle in the water.

cities.name: Savonlinna
cities.summary: A 15th-century castle on an island in the middle of Saimaa, which hosts opera in its courtyard each July.
highlights: Olavinlinna castle, built to face east and never taken by storm
Opera in the courtyard, one month a year
Saimaa ringed seals — a freshwater seal found nowhere else

experiences.name: Looking for the Saimaa seal
experiences.summary: Fewer than four hundred exist. A quiet boat, an early morning, and no promises — which is how it should be sold.

regions.name: Finnish Lapland
regions.summary: Above the Circle: fells rather than mountains, reindeer husbandry, and two months without a sunrise.

cities.name: Rovaniemi
cities.summary: The gateway to Lapland, rebuilt after 1944 to an Alvar Aalto plan shaped like reindeer antlers.
highlights: Arktikum, the best museum on Arctic life anywhere
Husky and reindeer trails from December to March
The Arctic Circle, marked and unavoidable

cities.name: Inari
cities.summary: The centre of Sámi Finland, on a lake with three thousand islands.
highlights: Siida: the Sámi museum, written by Sámi people
Ukonsaari, a sacred island out on the lake
Aurora with almost no light pollution in any direction

experiences.name: Siida, on Sámi terms
experiences.summary: A national minority telling its own story, including the parts about the Finnish state — worth an afternoon rather than an hour.
